model.name: Clinical / Biological Specimen
model.purpose: Represent one governed physical material specimen and its source-qualified collection, derivation, condition, custody, quality, use and disposition history.
model.scope_statement: Owns one physical specimen identity, accession and label bindings, profile and material classification; source references; direct material state and quantity; actual collection context; containers, additives and seals; parent-child, split, aliquot, pool, extraction, culture and transformation lineage; processing methods, devices, reagents and quantity effects; storage position and environment; transport and custody transitions; preanalytical variables, observations, quality, contamination, sufficiency and fitness assessments; availability, reservation, allocation, consumption, destruction and disposition; consent, permit and benefit-sharing bindings; provenance, correction, access, retention and loss-aware projections. Source organisms, people, environments, body sites, collection procedures, devices, containers, repositories, requests, observations, analyses, results, datasets, consent records, permits, agreements and decisions remain external.
in_scope: Physical specimen identity, material profile, source references, direct properties, quantity and collection context
Derivation, processing, containers, storage, transport, custody, quality, use and disposition history
Rights, consent and permit bindings, provenance, correction, access, retention and loss-aware interoperability
out_of_scope: Owning organism, person, environment, place, body site, procedure, device, container, repository, request, observation, assay, analysis, result, dataset, consent, permit, agreement or decision lifecycles
Inferring donor identity, disease, diagnosis, consent, ownership, fitness, quality or contamination status without source-qualified evidence
Protected disclosure, custody transfer, destructive use, physical disposal, external-system mutation or identity merge without authority

boundary_notes.distinction: The registered parent is retained as a common source reference. A specimen can also derive from another specimen, mixed organisms, environmental material, a place, substance or product, so organism parentage is not universal.
A repository owns collection policy, facilities, inventory services and holdings. It contains or controls specimens but does not become their physical identity or erase earlier custody.
An analysis consumes or observes specimen material and produces results or data. The specimen retains physical and derivation identity independently from request, assay and result.
The actual event creates or obtains the specimen from a source and is distinct from the order, planned procedure and physical material that remains afterward.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Container, label, accession and storage position
boundary_notes.distinction: These identify, contain or locate the specimen under a source system. Re-labeling, re-containerization or relocation never silently changes material identity.
Every aliquot, split, extract, culture or transformed output receives a new identity. A pool retains membership, contribution and quantity lineage to all source specimens.
Consent, lawful basis, collection permit, MTA, ABS terms and ownership or control are external governance records. Possession or custody does not prove title or permitted use.

dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint only Dimension-owned specimen, derivation, processing, placement, custody, quality and lifecycle assertion identifiers locally; preserve donor, organism, place, accession, container, repository, permit, analysis and result identifiers as typed external references.

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by registry ID, model version, authoritative physical-specimen identifier, profile, source-qualified boundary and immutable revision; never by donor name, accession display, barcode text, timestamp, container, position or hash alone.
Keep physical specimen, digital record, label, accession, container, source subject, collection event, repository holding, observation, assay, analysis, result, consent and decision distinct.
patch_rules: Additive extensions declare target node, specimen profile, authority, source, method, units, protocol and terminology releases, access, effective time and interoperability impact.

Breaking identity, derivation, quantity, custody, status or time changes require a new immutable revision, successor mapping, migration report, compatibility declaration and continued resolution of prior identifiers.
compatibility_rules: Consumers may ignore unknown additive fields only when specimen identity, physical boundary, source links, derivation, quantity, event clocks, custody and access meaning remain intact.
FHIR, MIABIS, NCBI BioSample, Phenopackets, Darwin Core, GGBN, MIxS and OBI mappings pin source and target releases and declare transformed, inferred, omitted or non-round-trippable values.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system specimen identifier or accession bound to one physical material entity.
Source-qualified immutable identifier for collection, derivation, processing, custody, quality or lifecycle assertion.
Adopting-Dimension UUID or ULID when no authoritative external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Record event timestamps in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; keep collection, receipt, accession, processing, storage, movement, custody, observation, reservation, consumption, destruction, correction and ingestion times distinct.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Name serial artifacts as {specimen-id}--{artifact-kind}--{revision-or-assertion-id}; never use donor name, sample label, date, barcode, container, position, filename or digest alone as identity.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, byte length, issuer, specimen and source identity, profile and rules versions, units, method, clocks, provenance, validation, sensitivity, consent or lawful basis, permit, purpose, access marking and semantic-loss declaration.

policies: The adopting Dimension declares who may register specimens, collect, label, process, derive, move, hold, assess, allocate, disclose, consume, destroy, correct and tombstone records.

Every usable specimen requires stable physical identity, explicit source context or unknown, material and profile classification, collection or derivation provenance, quantity and unit, status, custody and applicable governance.
Agents never infer donor identity, disease, diagnosis, consent, ownership, fitness, quality or absence of contamination from a label, specimen type, accession, container or repository record.

Organisms, people, environments, places, containers, devices, collection procedures, repositories, analyses, observations, results, datasets, consents, permits, agreements and decisions remain external masters.

Agents may validate identifiers, units, lineage, quantity balance and deterministic projections under delegation; collection, custody transfer, protected disclosure, destructive use, disposal and identity merge require accountable authority.

read: Resolve active Dimension, purpose, role, specimen identity and profile, source links, status, location, custody, quality, consent or lawful basis, permit, sensitivity, retention and access; return the minimum necessary projection.
create: Create a stable physical-specimen identity, profile, source context or explicit unknown, master authority, collection or derivation provenance and initial quantity before downstream processing is recorded.
update: Append an immutable collection, label, derivation, processing, placement, custody, quality, allocation, lifecycle or correction assertion with actor, authority, reason, source, method, RFC 3339 effective time and predecessor.
delete: Apply consent, permit, MTA, ABS, biosafety, clinical, legal, audit, retention and hold rules; tombstone eligible records or physically dispose material while preserving material provenance and non-cascading external masters.

access.default_rule: Deny protected human, genetic, sensitive-location, endangered-species or commercially restricted specimen context and mutation unless active Dimension, role, purpose, consent or lawful basis, permit, MTA, jurisdiction and field policy grant the action; expose the minimum necessary projection.

coverage.claim: WM-LIV-023 covers one governed physical clinical or biological specimen, source context, direct material properties, collection, containers, processing, derivation, quantity, storage, transport, custody, quality, use, disposition, rights, provenance and loss-aware interoperability. Specimen-type, assay, biosafety, species, jurisdictional and independent-review questions remain deferred.

checklist.notes: Physical specimen, record, accession, label, container, position, source, parent and child identities remain distinct.
Clinical, research, veterinary, plant, microbial, environmental, food and biodiversity profiles plus material types are explicit.
Material, physical state, composition, mass, volume, count, concentration, dimensions, container, additive and seal are source-qualified.
Agents distinguish specimens through authoritative identity, labels, physical boundaries, source links, container and custody evidence rather than a name alone.
Collect, label, derive, process, store, move, transfer, assess, allocate, consume, destroy and project actions expose authority and effects.
Available, reserved, allocated, partly consumed, depleted, destroyed, returned, disposed, corrected, merged and split states preserve history.
Source, parent-child, pool, container, repository, analysis, observation, consent, permit, agreement and result links are typed.
Collection, receipt, accession, processing, storage, movement, custody, observation, reservation, use, destruction and correction clocks remain distinct.
Source location, collection site, facility, unit, device, rack, box, slot, transport origin and destination are time-qualified.
Sources, actors, protocols, methods, devices, reagents, events, derivations, custody, observations, corrections and projections are linked.
Donor, source, owner, controller, custodian, possessor, collector, processor, repository and user roles are not conflated.
Identity collision, source match, label, lineage, quantity balance, time order, location, temperature, seal, quality and projection checks are explicit.
Consent or lawful basis, permits, MTA, ABS, purpose, role, jurisdiction, sensitivity, minimum projection and audit are represented.
Reservation, consumption, destruction, withdrawal, biosafety, legal hold, record continuity and non-cascading tombstones are explicit.
FHIR, MIABIS, BioSample, Phenopackets, Darwin Core, GGBN, MIxS and OBI projections pin releases and disclose loss.

known_omissions: Specimen-type, disease, assay, preservation, biosafety, dangerous-goods, species, clinical, biodiversity and jurisdiction profiles require expert review.

Source organisms, people, environments, places, devices, containers, procedures, repositories, observations, analyses, results, consents, permits, agreements, datasets and decisions remain neighboring masters.
Automated collection, diagnosis, fitness approval, access grant, custody transfer, destructive use and disposal remain outside unreviewed agent authority.
conflicts: Clinical specimen, biospecimen, biological sample, material sample, preserved specimen, isolate, aliquot and extract overlap across standards but have different boundaries and profiles.
Specimen identifier, accession, barcode, label, container identifier, storage position and digital record identifier cannot be collapsed into one universal identity.
FHIR, MIABIS, BioSample, Phenopackets, Darwin Core, GGBN, MIxS and OBI differ in scope, granularity, lifecycle and required provenance.
regional_assumptions: Human clinical requirements do not govern all veterinary, plant, microbial, environmental, food or biodiversity specimens.
ISO standards and ISBER practices include licensed or advisory material; exact releases and allowed use must be pinned before conformance claims.
Consent, privacy, access, benefit sharing, collection permits, biosafety, transport, retention and disposal depend on jurisdiction, species, material and purpose.
adversarial_checks: Reject a specimen without stable physical identity, master authority, material boundary, profile and collection or derivation provenance.
Reject donor name, sample label, accession display, barcode, container, storage position, timestamp or hash as universal material identity.
Reject child, aliquot, extract, culture or pool that overwrites parents, loses contributor identities or fails quantity reconciliation.
Reject planned request treated as actual collection or current location treated as custody or ownership.
Reject unqualified quality, fitness, contamination absence or diagnosis inferred from specimen type, label or repository metadata.
Reject consumption, destruction, disposal, merge, split or correction that erases prior material, quantity, evidence, consent, permit or custody history.
Reject protected human, genetic, sensitive-location or regulated-biological context disclosed without purpose, authority, minimum-necessary scope and audit.
